data.name: Espresso
data.description: Espresso is made by forcing hot water through finely ground coffee beans under high pressure. It uses a small amount of water and no milk, resulting in a strong, concentrated coffee with a rich flavor and a layer of foam (crema) on top. It is the base for many other coffee drinks.

data.name: Cappuccino
data.description: Cappuccino is prepared using equal parts espresso, steamed milk, and milk foam. First, a shot of espresso is brewed. Then steamed milk is added, followed by a thick layer of foam on top. It has a balanced taste with strong coffee flavor and creamy texture.

data.name: Latte
data.description: Latte is made with one shot of espresso and a larger amount of steamed milk, with a small layer of foam on top. The milk softens the strong coffee taste, making it smooth and creamy. It is less strong than cappuccino and great for beginners.

data.name: Americano
data.description: Americano is made by diluting a shot of espresso with hot water. It has a similar strength to drip coffee but retains the espresso's flavor. It is a popular choice for those who prefer a less intense coffee without milk.
